newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dubai's Dolphin expands into South African tourism.
newsitem.headline: Dubai's Dolphin expands into South African tourism.

text.p: The Dubai-based Dolphin Group on Thursday launched a joint venture company with South Africa's Mpumalanga Parks Board to capitalise on the province's prized ecotourism market.

Under the union between the parastatal and Dolphin, a major player in Africa's leisure industry through its Block Hotels and United Touring Company, the multinational takes over commercial running of the board's tourism and marketing divisions.

A primary objective of the 400 million rand joint venture is to ensure South Africa's youngest parks board can become self- sufficient despite progressively dwindling state funds, while keeping a tight rein over the region's rich natural heritage.
About 2,300 beds for theme camps and lodges are planned under the initial project which envisages four years of construction, with resultant spin-offs for the local building and service industries.

New developments will centre on the historic mining town of Pilgrim's Rest, the Blyde river canyon -- a massive red sandstone gorge with cliff faces plunging 700 metres in parts -- the Loskop dam reserve, Songimvelo and Manyaleti game reserves.
Up to 2,000 jobs are expected to be generated, vital to the region's struggling economy.
The parks board currently operates an annual budget of around 55 million rand from the government, but has had to find an alternative source of income as budget cuts loom.
"There is definitely a depleting budget for conservation," parks board chief executive Alan Gray told reporters, adding private sector intervention had become essential to conservation.

"If these areas are not developed for the benefit of neighbouring communities, then the integrity of these reserves will most certainly be threatened, and they could in fact be lost forever," Gray said.

Built into the deal reached with Dolphin, Gray said, was an agreement that local communities and entrepreneurs living on the borders of the parks would be given a 20 percent shareholding in the development companies to be formed in the five target areas.
The first shareholding had already been set aside in the Songimvelo reserve.
Block Hotels also announced on Thursday that it would invest in two Johannesburg hotels in line with its policy of targeting key arrival cities.
Based in the upmarket suburb of Sandton, both would be five-star products.
Block Hotels chairman John Small told reporters he was assessing expansion into South Africa's other tourist cities.
"We're looking at properties in Cape Town. Essentially we'll be looking at Durban as well when the airports are finished in this part of the world.
"We need places for people to come, arrive, overnight and from there go onto their vacation. So we have to have properties in these key destination cities," said Small.
